macro.headline: Indices grind up, but internals split as tech fades and defensives rotate in.
macro.story:
The facts first: SPY closed at 754.81, up 0.4% on the day and 2.0% over 21 days, above both its 50- and 200-day averages with RSI at 58.4 and MACD above signal — a healthy but not extended tape. QQQ tells a different story, RSI at 50.0, MACD below signal, and 21-day return slightly negative (-0.4%) despite being above key averages. VIX printed 16.28 (+3.9% on the day, +2.8% over 5 days) — still low, but rising. Breadth is mixed: 6 of 11 GICS sectors above their 50-day, S&P 500 breadth at 35.9% bullish vs 21.1% bearish, and DXY firming at 100.5 while gold (-6.8% over 21d) and silver (-18.8% over 21d) are getting hit hard. WTI is up 11.3% over 5 days to $80.22. The Engine C washout state reads CALM: SPY sits 9% above its 200-day with RSI at 58.4 — no washout signal engaged.

The prevailing sentiment in the tracked conversation attributes today's cross-currents to a handful of specific narratives rather than one clean driver. The dominant thread is a memory-chip unwind — Micron's two-day drop of roughly 15% is being flagged as an accelerating selloff, with chart reads highlighting a persistent lower-highs pattern into support near $850–$860. The second thread is Big-Tech credit stress: sentiment is pointing to 5-year CDS spreads on names like Oracle widening to roughly 75bp, the highest in seven years, as evidence that institutional risk perception is quietly shifting even while headline indices grind higher. The third thread — bullish-leaning — is Q2 earnings strength, led by UnitedHealth's +8% post-print move. On energy, sentiment is flagging China crude imports collapsing -41% YoY as a demand-side warning that conflicts with the price action (WTI +11% over 5 days), which the tracked conversation attributes to geopolitical relief (Iran/Hormuz) per the active themes data — not live sentiment. The lean is genuinely mixed: bullish voices point to earnings and energy strength, bearish voices point to memory, mega-cap credit risk and stretched leveraged-ETF positioning. This tension aligns with the sector data — Financials and Communication Services leading, Technology and Nasdaq-100 tagged BEARISH by the momentum score.

Rotation-wise, the validated Early-Runway signal is firing across ten industries dominated by Healthcare (Diagnostics & Research, Health Information Services, Drug Manufacturers), Financials (Credit Services, Staffing), Energy (Refining & Marketing) and Communication Services (Internet Content, Advertising) — all early in their hot spells (roughly 12–25% through a typical run) with top-decile RS. This is a genuine, statistically-confirmed rotation tailwind and it maps cleanly onto the sector momentum table where Financials, Communication Services and Energy carry the top scores, while Technology and Materials sit at the bottom.

Forward watch: does the memory-chip weakness spread to broader semis and drag QQQ (already MACD-bearish) below its 50-day? Does the CDS-spread widening the tracked sentiment is flagging show up in mega-cap equity price? Does the DXY firming continue to pressure gold/silver (validated inverse relationship)? Confidence is capped at MEDIUM: trend, momentum, and vol context conflict — SPY constructive but QQQ weakening, VIX rising off lows, breadth only moderate, and the sentiment narrative is genuinely split.

newsletter:
**[THE SPINE]** The AI infrastructure trade remains the dominant force this week, but it is bifurcating — the leaders (Semiconductors +258% over 13 months) are hitting ceiling territory while the second-derivative names (Software - Infrastructure, Internet Content) are just entering their first month of heat. The tape is not broad; it is a rotation *within* the AI complex from run-extended chip names into adjacent infrastructure and hyperscaler-adjacent software.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop is permissive but not confirming. Regime prints CHOPPY at 6/10 with a TRANSITIONAL vote, VIX at 16.23 in contango (VIX3M 18.57) — no vol stress. SPY RSI 58.4 is trending, not overbought, and we do not fade it (backtest: no edge). Yields are the friction: 10Y at 4.59% with RSI 59.4 and 21d +2.7% — trending higher, and we make no ceiling call there (backtest: DOESN'T HOLD, yields kept rising 53% of the time after prior 'ceiling' signals). DXY at 100.54 is mixed vs its SMAs (DXY_METALS_TAG: HOLDS, no clean call yet), but Gold -7.6%/21d and Silver -19.8%/21d confirm the DXY/metals inverse is doing real damage. Precious metals theme is officially FADING.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS cont.]** Bond posture matters for the spine: TLT at 84.24, RSI 39.6, 21d -1.4%. We do not call TLT oversold-reversion (backtest: DOESN'T HOLD). Rising yields + falling long bonds is a headwind for long-duration growth multiples — which is exactly why leadership is narrowing within AI rather than broadening to unprofitable tech.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** XLF leads at +6.4%/21d (steepening curve, regional banks stabilizing), XLV +3.4%, XLI +2.5%. Notably, QQQ is -0.4%/21d and XLY +0.5% — the Nasdaq-100 is *lagging* while individual AI-adjacent industries accelerate. Rotation is INTO Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and an unmapped bucket (likely AI power/compute infra). Nothing rotating out cleanly — this is accumulation into new leadership, not distribution.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The extended side is Semiconductors: 13 months hot, +258% (the largest run on record, ceiling flag active). NVDA shows up coiled at 91% with bullish flow, but this is exit management territory, not fresh entries — respect the ceiling. The in-range opportunity sits in Software - Infrastructure, month one of heat with only +3% booked vs typical +18% and record +93%: **NTAP** (coil 91.3%, bullish flow), **PLTR** (coil 84.1%, bullish flow), **XYZ** (coil 89.0%, lean bullish). These are the un-run names inside the spine. Internet Content and Internet Retail are also month-one with room, but flows aren't as clean.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The tripwire is SPY 758.45 resistance against the 10Y at 4.59%. If SPY breaks 758 while 10Y pushes through 4.69% res, the AI spine survives the yield backup and Software - Infra names get their extension. If SPY fails 758 AND 10Y clears 4.69%, duration pain forces a de-rating of the second-derivative AI names before they can run, and the ceiling on Semis becomes the whole tape's ceiling. Secondary watch: DXY resolution above 101.8 or below 100.56 — clean trend either way changes the metals fade and the risk-on tone.
